items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: Yeah. He spent some good years with Ray Charles.

ctx.x: Oh no. No it was a very secular thing. We knew those people but, in fact I even divided it up even more than that. The people who don’t listen to the blues because it’s the devil’s music or something like that, still have a body of secular music that, that’s part of their life too. You know you could say it’s folksy or something like that. But you know when you hear people like King Curtis or “Fathead” Newman, that is David Newman, (we don’t want to call him “Fathead” on this) — I worked with him the last two…
Yeah. He spent some good years with Ray Charles.

Ray Charles. And there’s a difference between when he’s playing his down home thing that’s not the blues and if you listen to my latest CD you’ll find a piece called “Little Black Lucille.” “Little black Lucille was an aunt of mine who definitely wouldn’t want to be on a blues record. And she never heard this tune being played with a rhythm section and everything. I used to play it for her on the whistle and she liked it very much.
